CALIFORNIA ESCROW LAW — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for 123 Main St, Apt 4, Springfield · Pat Morgan

ABOUT THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes California's Escrow Law, Financial Code sections 17000 through 17703, which regulates escrow agents — the licensed corporations that hold funds, documents, and instructions for property transactions on behalf of others. It is prepared in connection with a transaction involving the property at 123 Main St, Apt 4, Springfield, between Pat Morgan and Jordan Lee. This sheet states what the statute says about who must be licensed as an escrow agent, who is exempt, what escrow instructions generally must contain, and how escrowed funds must be handled. It does not recommend which escrow provider to use, does not evaluate any particular escrow agent's compliance, and is not a substitute for the escrow instructions governing this specific transaction.

WHAT "ESCROW" AND "ESCROW AGENT" MEAN UNDER THE STATUTE
The Escrow Law defines "escrow" as a transaction in which one person delivers a written instrument, money, evidence of title, or other thing of value to a third person, to be held until a specified event happens or a condition is performed and then delivered to the party entitled to it. An "escrow agent" is any person engaged in the business of receiving escrows for deposit or delivery, and a "licensee" is any person holding a valid, unrevoked license as an escrow agent. These definitions describe the function performed, not any particular job title — a person who receives and holds funds or documents this way for a property transaction is acting as an escrow agent under the statute regardless of what they call themselves.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "“Escrow” means any transaction in which one person, for the purpose of effecting the sale, transfer, encumbering, or leasing of real or personal property to another person, delivers any written instrument, money, evidence of title to real or personal property, or other thing of value to a third person to be held by that third person until the happening of a specified event or the performance of a prescribed condition, when it is then to be delivered by that third person to a grantee, grantor, promisee, promisor, obligee, obligor, bailee, bailor, or any agent or employee of any of the latter."
  — Cal. Fin. Code § 17003(a) (leginfo text), Financial Code § 17003(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=FIN&division=6.&title=&part=&chapter=1.&article=)
  "“Escrow agent” means any person engaged in the business of receiving escrows for deposit or delivery."
  — Cal. Fin. Code § 17004 (leginfo text), Financial Code § 17004 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=FIN&division=6.&title=&part=&chapter=1.&article=)
  "“Licensee” means any person holding a valid, unrevoked license as an escrow agent."
  — Cal. Fin. Code § 17005 (leginfo text), Financial Code § 17005 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=FIN&division=6.&title=&part=&chapter=1.&article=)
  Known gap: The statutory definition of "escrow" in Section 17003(a) is written broadly around real or personal property transactions generally; Section 17003(b) separately extends the term to certain Internet-based transactions in personal property or services, a variant this clause does not detail because it falls outside a real-property escrow context. Also, meeting this functional definition does not by itself determine whether a license is required — that depends on whether one of the statutory exemptions applies, which is addressed in a separate clause.

LICENSING REQUIREMENT FOR ESCROW AGENTS
California law makes it unlawful for a person to engage in business as an escrow agent within the state except through a corporation organized for that purpose and licensed by the Commissioner of Financial Protection and Innovation. A licensed escrow agent corporation must also deposit and maintain a bond — at least $25,000, and more depending on the size of its trust fund obligations — as a condition of holding the license.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "It shall be unlawful for any person to engage in business as an escrow agent within this state except by means of a corporation duly organized for that purpose licensed by the commissioner as an escrow agent."
  — Cal. Fin. Code § 17200 (leginfo text), Financial Code § 17200 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=FIN&division=6.&title=&part=&chapter=2.&article=)
  "At the time of filing an application for an escrow agent’s license, the applicant shall deposit with the commissioner a bond satisfactory to the commissioner in the amount of at least twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000)."
  — Cal. Fin. Code § 17202(a) (leginfo text), Financial Code § 17202(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=FIN&division=6.&title=&part=&chapter=2.&article=)
  Known gap: This clause states the general licensing rule; it does not cover the statute's separate exemption list, which removes certain categories of persons from the licensing requirement entirely for escrow work performed within their own exempt capacity — that is addressed in a separate clause. It also does not describe the corporation's other ongoing licensing conditions (minimum tangible net worth, qualified-personnel staffing, and periodic examination by the Commissioner), which this sheet does not exhaustively catalog.

PERSONS EXEMPT FROM THE ESCROW AGENT LICENSE REQUIREMENT
The Escrow Law does not apply to certain categories of persons handling property transactions in their own separate capacity: banks, trust companies, building and loan or savings and loan associations, credit unions, and insurance companies; an attorney licensed to practice law in California who has a bona fide client relationship with a principal in the transaction and who is not actively engaged in the business of an escrow agent; a person whose principal business is preparing abstracts or title searches used as the basis for a title insurance policy; and a real estate broker performing acts in the course of, or incidental to, a real estate transaction in which the broker is an agent or party and is performing an act for which a real estate license is required. None of these exempt categories needs a separate escrow license to handle funds or documents within that described role. The person invoking an exemption carries the burden of proving it applies.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(a) This division does not apply to: (1) Any person doing business under any law of this state or the United States relating to banks, trust companies, building and loan or savings and loan associations, credit unions, or insurance companies. (2) Any person licensed to practice law in California who has a bona fide client relationship with a principal in a real estate or personal property transaction and who is not actively engaged in the business of an escrow agent. (3) Any person whose principal business is that of preparing abstracts or making searches of title that are used as a basis for the issuance of a policy of title insurance by a company doing business under any law of this state relating to insurance companies. (4) Any broker licensed by the Real Estate Commissioner while performing acts in the course of or incidental to a real estate transaction in which the broker is an agent or a party to the transaction and in which the broker is performing an act for which a real estate license is required."
  — Cal. Fin. Code § 17006(a) (leginfo text), Financial Code § 17006(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=FIN&division=6.&title=&part=&chapter=1.&article=)
  "(b) The exemptions provided for in paragraphs (2) and (4) of subdivision (a) are personal to the persons listed, and those persons shall not delegate any duties other than duties performed under the direct supervision of those persons. Notwithstanding the provisions of this subdivision, the exemptions provided for in paragraphs (2) and (4) of subdivision (a) are not available for any arrangement entered into for the purpose of performing escrows for more than one business."
  — Cal. Fin. Code § 17006(b) (leginfo text), Financial Code § 17006(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=FIN&division=6.&title=&part=&chapter=1.&article=)
  "In any proceeding under this law, the burden of proving an exemption or an exception from a definition is upon the person claiming it."
  — Cal. Fin. Code § 17006.5 (leginfo text), Financial Code § 17006.5 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=FIN&division=6.&title=&part=&chapter=1.&article=)
  Known gap: The attorney and real estate broker exemptions are narrower than a blanket profession-based exemption: the statute itself labels them "personal to the persons listed," meaning that person cannot delegate the exempt escrow work to others (beyond staff under their own direct supervision), and neither exemption is available at all for an arrangement entered into for the purpose of performing escrows for more than one business. The title-company exemption likewise applies only to the specific business of preparing abstracts or title searches underlying a title policy, not to title companies generally. This sheet cannot determine whether a given attorney, broker, or title company's actual conduct in a particular transaction stays within its exempt role or crosses into operating an unlicensed escrow business — that is a case-by-case factual question the statute leaves to be proven.

HOW ESCROW INSTRUCTIONS FUNCTION UNDER THE STATUTE
The statute regulates the mechanics of escrow instructions themselves, not just who may act as an escrow agent. An escrow agent may not solicit or accept an escrow instruction containing a blank to be filled in after it is signed or initialed, and no addition, deletion, or alteration may be made afterward unless it is signed or initialed by everyone who signed or initialed the original. A copy of each executed escrow instruction, and of any amendment or supplement, must be delivered to everyone who executed it. And every written escrow instruction executed by a buyer or seller — whether prepared by a licensed escrow agent or by a person exempt under Section 17006, such as an attorney or real estate broker — must contain a statement, in not less than 10-point type, identifying the license name and the department issuing the license or authority under which the preparer is operating.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "No person subject to this division shall solicit or accept an escrow instruction or amended or supplemental escrow instruction containing any blank to be filled in after signing or initialing of the escrow instruction or amended or supplemental escrow instruction, nor permit any person to make any addition to, deletion from, or alteration of an escrow instruction or amended or supplemental escrow instruction, unless the addition, deletion or alteration is signed or initialed by all persons who had signed or initialed the escrow instruction or amended or supplemental escrow instruction prior to the addition, deletion or alteration."
  — Cal. Fin. Code § 17403.2(a) (leginfo text), Financial Code § 17403.2(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=FIN&division=6.&title=&part=&chapter=3.&article=)
  "At the time of execution a copy of each escrow instruction or amended or supplemental escrow instruction shall be delivered to all persons executing the same."
  — Cal. Fin. Code § 17403.3(a) (leginfo text), Financial Code § 17403.3(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=FIN&division=6.&title=&part=&chapter=3.&article=)
  "All written escrow instructions and all escrow instructions transmitted electronically over the Internet executed by a buyer or seller, whether prepared by a person subject to this division or by a person exempt from this division under Section 17006, shall contain a statement in not less than 10-point type which shall include the license name and the name of the department issuing the license or authority under which the person is operating."
  — Cal. Fin. Code § 17403.4 (leginfo text), Financial Code § 17403.4 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=FIN&division=6.&title=&part=&chapter=3.&article=)
  Known gap: The 10-point-type disclosure requirement in Section 17403.4 does not apply to supplemental escrow instructions or modifications to escrow instructions, so a later amendment to instructions for a particular property transaction is not independently required to repeat that disclosure. This clause describes the instructions' required form and delivery; it does not address their substantive content requirements (such as what escrow instructions must specify about the terms of closing), which the statute leaves largely to what the commissioner's regulations and the parties' own agreement require rather than prescribing in the text reviewed here.

TRUST-FUND HANDLING REQUIREMENTS
Money deposited in escrow to be delivered at closing or on another contingency must be deposited and maintained in a noninterest-bearing demand or checking account (or a qualifying noninterest-bearing account subject to immediate withdrawal) at a bank, state or federal savings institution, or an approved industrial loan company. Funds may later be moved to an interest-bearing account only if kept separate, distinct, and apart from the escrow agent's own funds. Deposited funds must be designated as "trust funds," "escrow accounts," or some other appropriate name showing they do not belong to the escrow agent. The statute reinforces that separation by making escrow or trust funds unreachable by a money judgment against the escrow agent and by providing that such funds are never to be treated as an asset of the escrow agent, and separately by making it unlawful to knowingly keep funds under a "trust funds" or "escrow accounts" label unless they are actual escrow or trust funds.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "All moneys deposited in escrow to be delivered upon the close of the escrow or upon any other contingency shall be deposited and maintained in a noninterest-bearing demand or checking account in a bank, a state or federal savings bank, or a state or federal savings association or in a noninterest-bearing account subject to immediate withdrawal in an industrial loan company insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation and approved to receive those moneys by the commissioner."
  — Cal. Fin. Code § 17409(a) (leginfo text), Financial Code § 17409(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=FIN&division=6.&title=&part=&chapter=3.&article=)
  "Escrow or trust funds are not subject to enforcement of a money judgment arising out of any claim against the licensee or person acting as escrow agent, and in no instance shall such escrow or trust funds be considered or treated as an asset of the licensee or person performing the functions of an escrow agent."
  — Cal. Fin. Code § 17410(a) (leginfo text), Financial Code § 17410(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=FIN&division=6.&title=&part=&chapter=3.&article=)
  "No person shall knowingly keep or cause to be kept any funds or money in any bank or state or federal savings and loan association under the heading of “trust funds” or “escrow accounts” or any other name designating such funds or money as belonging to the clients of any escrow agency, except actual escrow or trust funds deposited with such agency."
  — Cal. Fin. Code § 17411 (leginfo text), Financial Code § 17411 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=FIN&division=6.&title=&part=&chapter=3.&article=)
  Known gap: These trust-fund handling rules govern licensed escrow agents and persons otherwise subject to the division; the statute defines "trust funds" and "escrow accounts," for purposes of these sections, to include all funds an escrow agent is required to hold under any federal or state law or governmental-agency requirement, which is broader than only funds received directly in a transaction's escrow. This clause does not address the separate, more detailed requirements for maintaining distinct trust accounts by licensed location and by escrow type (Sections 17409(b) and 17409.1), which go beyond the general deposit and labeling rules described here.

CONSEQUENCES FOR MISAPPROPRIATING ESCROW FUNDS OR OPERATING WITHOUT A LICENSE
The Escrow Law backs its trust-fund and licensing rules with penalties. A director, officer, stockholder, trustee, employee, or agent of an escrow agent who abstracts or willfully misappropriates money, funds, trust obligations, or property deposited with an escrow agent is guilty of a felony. More generally, a person who willfully violates any provision of the Escrow Law, or any rule or order issued under it, is subject on conviction to a fine of up to $10,000, imprisonment in county jail for up to one year (or, in some cases, imprisonment under Penal Code section 1170(h)), or both. The statute also authorizes a separate civil penalty of up to $2,500 per violation, recoverable by the Commissioner in a civil action, and states that these remedies are not exclusive of one another.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Any director, officer, stockholder, trustee, employee, or agent of an escrow agent, who abstracts or willfully misappropriates money, funds, trust obligations or property deposited with an escrow agent, is guilty of a felony."
  — Cal. Fin. Code § 17414(b) (leginfo text), Financial Code § 17414(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=FIN&division=6.&title=&part=&chapter=3.&article=)
  "Any person who willfully violates any provision of this division, or who willfully violates any rule or order under this division, shall, upon conviction, be fined not more than ten thousand dollars ($10,000), imprisoned in a county jail for not more than one year, imprisoned pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170 of the Penal Code, or be punished by both that fine and imprisonment, but no person may be imprisoned for the violation of any rule or order unless he or she had knowledge of the rule or order."
  — Cal. Fin. Code § 17700 (leginfo text), Financial Code § 17700 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=FIN&division=6.&title=&part=&chapter=7.&article=)
  "Any person who violates any provision of this division, or who violates any rule or order under this division, shall be liable for a civil penalty not to exceed two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500) for each violation, which shall be assessed and recovered in a civil action brought in the name of the people of the State of California by the commissioner in any court of competent jurisdiction."
  — Cal. Fin. Code § 17701(a) (leginfo text), Financial Code § 17701(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=FIN&division=6.&title=&part=&chapter=7.&article=)
  Known gap: This clause describes the penalty provisions found in the text reviewed; it does not describe every enforcement tool available to the Commissioner (for example, license suspension or revocation proceedings, or the Commissioner's separate authority to order a person to desist from unlicensed escrow activity), which operate independently of these criminal and civil penalty sections. A CourtListener case-law search to confirm how these penalty provisions have actually been applied or interpreted by California courts could not be completed for this sheet: CourtListener's daily search quota (125 requests/day) was already exhausted when checked, so no case law is cited here — this clause relies on the statutory text alone.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT
This information sheet was prepared for reference in connection with the transaction involving 123 Main St, Apt 4, Springfield and does not itself constitute escrow instructions, a legal opinion, or advice about which escrow arrangement to use. Prepared and reviewed as of September 1, 2026, at Oakland, California.
